name: Paired Fall
observation:
Six abnormally bright stars sit in the sky in a single straight rising line - a staircase - unmistakably brighter and larger than the 900-2600 background stars, and unmistakably NOT part of the drifting star field (they are parented to `group`, not to `sky`, exactly like the moon, so they never move). Fixed placement, radius 44m, altitudes 26/34/42/50/58/66 degrees and azimuths 87/71/55/39/23/7 degrees (bottom of the chain to top), the whole chain rotated by a seeded azimuth offset. These altitudes clear the glazing cage's three latitude rings (21.8/45.8/69.9 deg) by >=3.8 deg and every beacon clears the 12 cage ribs (azimuth multiples of 30 deg) by >=2.5 deg of sky angle, and the lowest sits 5 deg above the dome's painted horizon haze.

Over a 20.00 s loop, meteors arrive in TWOS. Each burst is two streaks entering from different seeded bearings, each sweeping a 35 deg arc of sky in 1.10 s, and each DYING exactly on one of the six chain stars - it does not pass through, it terminates there. The two stars it hit then jump to full brightness and HOLD lit for 3.00 s while the other four sit at base. So at any moment between bursts, exactly two of the six are lit, and which two changes four times per loop.

Timeline (phase = elapsed mod 20.00): 0.00 streaks 1 launch; 1.10 pair 1 lit; 4.10 release + streaks 2 launch; 5.20 pair 2 lit; 8.20 release + streaks 3; 9.30 pair 3 lit; 12.30 release + streaks 4; 13.40 pair 4 lit; 16.40 release, then the WHOLE CHAIN FADES TO 15% for 3.60 s and comes back up. That blackout is the loop marker and is 3x longer than the 1.10 s streak-flight gaps, and darker than them (during flight the chain sits at base, during the blackout at 15%), so it is never confusable with them.

Crucially the loop's ORDER is phase-invariant: any observer, whenever they mounted, sees blackout -> pair A -> pair B -> pair C -> pair D -> blackout. Two players doubled into this chamber with different mount times still read the same sequence, so no server clock is needed - pure `elapsed` + seed satisfies the cross-client requirement.
deduction:
Three things, in order, and only the first is the big one.

1. THE CHAIN IS THE CATALOGUE. The six bright stars are unlabelled. The parapet frieze names six stars on six numbered plates - 01 THUBAN +64d22', 02 ALKAID +49d19', 03 SADR +40d15', 04 MENKAR +04d05', 05 KEID -07d39', 06 ACRUX -63d06' - already ordered, descending. The chain in the sky is also ordered, by height. Six and six, both sorted, one line each. The top of the chain is plate 01, the bottom is plate 06. This is the "oh, THAT's what's happening" - and it is self-verifying without a scrap of astronomy, because the plate values run from PLUS sixty-four down to MINUS sixty-three and plus reads as up, minus as down. A player who maps the chain upside down gets a wholly different answer, and the signs are what stop them.

2. THE PAIRING IS THE LIT PAIR. Meteors are what make the pairing, and the 3.00 s hold is what makes it readable - you don't need reflexes, you need to look at the chain and see which two are burning. Because the chain is monotone, "the upper of the two" is instantly unambiguous, and equals the smaller plate number.

3. THE ORDER IS THE LOOP. Four falls, logged from the blackout.

Conversion (stated as instrument procedure on the Fragment, since a letter-indexing convention is arbitrary and could not be discovered by looking - the DEDUCTION is steps 1-3, not this): each of a fall's two plates yields one letter, by counting into THAT plate's name by the OTHER plate's number. So a fall linking 02 ALKAID and 04 MENKAR yields ALKAID's 4th letter (A) and MENKAR's 2nd letter (E). Every fall therefore hands the player two candidate letters and no way at all to choose between them. Four falls = an upper string and a lower string, 16 possible readings, and the room contains nothing that resolves it.
neighbourKeyRole: Key kind `sides`, label TRACK READ, value e.g. `LOW-HIGH-HIGH-LOW`. For each fall in loop order it says whether to log the UPPER plate or the LOWER plate of that pair. It is four bits. It names no star, no letter, no position and no order - printed on its own it is literally four words with nothing to apply them to, so a player who is handed it without doing the work has gained nothing. Conversely the observer who has done all the work still holds two full candidate strings and cannot pick between them: the generator rejects any pair whose upper and lower letters are equal, so the key is load-bearing on EVERY fall, not just some. Sixteen blind attempts against LOCKOUT_MS = 30_000 is up to eight minutes of dead time, so brute-forcing past the neighbour is not a strategy. This is the required shape exactly: genuine thinking either side of the key, and the key gates how to read the deduction rather than being it.
seededValues: The four falls: four DISTINCT unordered plate pairs drawn from the 10 legal pairs - (1,2)(1,4)(1,5)(1,6)(2,3)(2,4)(2,6)(3,4)(4,5)(4,6). The other five are illegal because the index overruns the partner's name (SADR and KEID are only 4 letters) or because the letter produced is I, O or S, which the answer-format rule bans. 10x9x8x7 = 5040 orderings.
The order the four falls occupy in the loop (already counted above).
The four TRACK READ sides, one bit per fall: 16 combinations. Total puzzle space 5040 x 16 = 80,640, so nothing is memorisable or shareable between playthroughs.

The chain's whole-azimuth offset, drawn from {0,30,60,90,120,180,210,240,270,300,330} degrees. Multiples of 30 preserve the cage-rib clearance exactly; 150 is excluded because it drops ACRUX onto the moon at azimuth 235 / altitude 26. Prevents 'the top-right one is always THUBAN'.

Each of the eight meteors' approach bearing around its terminal star, constrained so the two streaks of a burst enter >=60 degrees apart and so the whole 35-degree track stays between 25 and 85 degrees altitude (never below the dome's haze band, never through the zenith rib convergence).

geometryChanges.change: Six catalogue beacons. One THREE.Points, 6 vertices, PointsMaterial({map: getMoteSprite(), size: 0.75, sizeAttenuation: true, vertexColors: true, transparent: true, blending: AdditiveBlending, depthWrite: false, fog: false}), radius 44m. Added to `group`, NEVER to `sky` - the file's own moon comment is the precedent: information that drifts is information nobody can quote. Size 0.75 at 44m is ~0.98 deg, 3.4x the field stars' 0.24 deg and far under the moon's 12.8 deg. Base colour ~0.42 grey-white, lit 1.0 white: a 2.4x additive pop that reads as a flare without clipping to a white blob.

Meteor streaks. One THREE.Mesh, BufferGeometry of 8 vertices / 4 triangles (two camera-facing ribbons), MeshBasicMaterial({vertexColors, transparent, blending: AdditiveBlending, depthWrite: false, fog: false}). Head opaque, 8-degree tail faded to zero via vertex alpha - no texture. Only ever two streaks alive at once. Ribbon width axis is cross(travelDir, viewDir), cheap because the camera is pinned at (0,1.62,0).

update(dt, elapsed) additions: phase = elapsed % 20.00; write 18 beacon colour floats and 24 streak position floats per frame. Pure functions of phase + the seeded burst table, zero allocation, no Math.random at play time. Existing ring/alidade/sky/panel animation is untouched - the puzzle carries its own 20 s cycle and needs no re-timing, so do not touch ringSpinners, alidade.rotation.y or sky.rotation.y.

makeFriezeAtlas(): the plate index numeral goes from '400 22px' at rgba(196,206,228,0.42) to '600 34px' at rgba(226,232,246,0.85). The number is now load-bearing (it is the letter position), and at 22px/0.42 alpha it is ~13px tall and half-transparent from the pier. At 34px it is ~0.095m of plate, ~1.19 deg, ~20px at 1080p - as legible as the star name beside it.

Plumbing: createObservatory({dimensions}) becomes createObservatory({dimensions, puzzlePrompt}) and scenes.js createRoom(id, options) forwards it. The room needs prompt.bursts and prompt.chainOffsetDeg to render at all. This leaks nothing: prompt carries the pairs, key carries the sides, answer is never serialised - a client that reads its own prompt gets both candidate strings and still cannot choose.
geometryChanges.cost: 0 draw calls; one field through scenes.js

fragmentBrief:
PAIRED FALL — LOGGING PROCEDURE

Falls arrive in twos. A fall is logged as the two
catalogue plates it ends on.

Each plate gives up ONE letter: count into that
plate's NAME by the OTHER plate's number.

    ▣ NN ─────────╮
    ▢▢▢▢▢▢        │  count in by the
        ╰─────────╯  partner's number

One letter per fall, logged in the order the
falls occur.

WHICH plate of the two you log is set by the
TRACK READ, held next door.

[The small canvas diagram uses blank plate boxes and a placeholder "NN", never a real name or number, so it teaches the counting convention and nothing else. The brief never says the bright chain is the catalogue, never says how to tell one plate's star from another, never says where the loop starts, and never says which side to take.]
exampleWalkthrough:
SEED: chain offset +60 deg. Falls in loop order: {02,04}, {01,06}, {03,04}, {01,05}. TRACK READ = LOW-HIGH-HIGH-LOW (held in the Vault). Answer = ENRK, never sent to any client.

Sky as rendered: THUBAN az 67/alt 66, ALKAID az 83/alt 58, SADR az 99/alt 50, MENKAR az 115/alt 42, KEID az 131/alt 34, ACRUX az 147/alt 26.

1. The player watches. Six bright stars in a clean rising line. Meteors keep arriving two at a time and dying on two of them, which stay burning for three seconds. Then the whole line goes dark for three and a half seconds and it starts over.

2. Opens the Fragment: "a fall is logged as the two catalogue plates it ends on." Turns to the parapet.

3. The frieze: 01 THUBAN +64d22', 02 ALKAID +49d19', 03 SADR +40d15', 04 MENKAR +04d05', 05 KEID -07d39', 06 ACRUX -63d06'. Six plates, descending, plus at the top and minus at the bottom. Six stars, one line, descending. Top of the chain is 01 THUBAN. Bottom is 06 ACRUX. That is the whole trick.

4. Logs one loop from the blackout:
   fall 1 - 2nd and 4th from the top lit -> ALKAID 02, MENKAR 04
   fall 2 - top and bottom lit -> THUBAN 01, ACRUX 06
   fall 3 - 3rd and 4th lit -> SADR 03, MENKAR 04
   fall 4 - top and 5th lit -> THUBAN 01, KEID 05

5. Converts, counting into each name by the partner's number:
   fall 1: ALKAID by 4 -> A-L-K-[A] = A (upper) | MENKAR by 2 -> M-[E] = E (lower)
   fall 2: THUBAN by 6 -> T-H-U-B-A-[N] = N (upper) | ACRUX by 1 -> [A] = A (lower)
   fall 3: SADR by 4 -> S-A-D-[R] = R (upper) | MENKAR by 3 -> M-E-[N] = N (lower)
   fall 4: THUBAN by 5 -> T-H-U-B-[A] = A (upper) | KEID by 1 -> [K] = K (lower)
   The room has now given up everything it has: upper string ANRA, lower string EANK. Sixteen readings. Nothing in this chamber can choose.

6. Calls the Vault. "TRACK READ: low, high, high, low."

7. fall 1 LOW = E. fall 2 HIGH = N. fall 3 HIGH = R. fall 4 LOW = K. Types ENRK into the Answer Lock. Four letters, no I, no O, no S, and "echo november romeo kilo" survives a voice call.
difficultyNotes:
Why a 13-year-old gets there. Every step is a primary-school operation dressed as an instrument. Sort six things by height. Match them to six things already sorted on a wall. Count to the fourth letter of a word. The one number-literacy demand is reading +64 as higher than -63, and the signs do that work on their own - no declination, no ephemeris, no cipher, no outside knowledge of any kind. Nothing needs clicking: you stand on the pier, turn, look up, look down at the frieze, type. And the 3.00 s hold means it never tests reflexes - a player who blinks through a burst waits 20 s and gets it again, forever.

What stops it being instant. (a) You cannot answer without watching at least one full loop, and realistically two or three - one to notice falls come in twos, one to find the blackout and fix the order, one to check the pairs you half-saw. (b) The identification is a real leap: six unlabelled lights and six named plates, and the ONLY bridge is that both lists are sorted. Nothing in the room states it, and the Fragment deliberately does not. (c) Direction is a live trap - map the chain bottom-up and you get a clean, confident, completely wrong four letters. The plus/minus signs are the check, and finding that check is part of the puzzle. (d) The last step cannot be reached alone. Sixteen candidate strings, no tell, and the file's own 30-second lockout makes guessing your way past your neighbour cost up to eight minutes.

Honest risks for the builder to watch in playtest. The rings at radius 2.55-3.55 sweep across the sky as ~1.5-2 deg hairlines and will briefly cross a beacon; this is momentary and the beacon holds for three seconds, so it should cost nothing, but it is the thing to watch first. And at 62 deg vertical FOV the chain's ~68 deg diagonal extent does not quite fit one screen at the widest offsets - the 3.00 s hold is what covers the pan, so if playtest says it feels rushed, lengthen the hold and the loop toward the 25 s ceiling rather than compressing the chain.
